chunks: And with this chain of narrators, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan, from Saif al-Tammār, that he said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Sa'id ibn Abd al-Malik arrived as a pilgrim and met my father (peace be upon him) and said: I brought an offering animal, so what should I do? He said: Feed your family one third, feed the contented one third, and feed the beggar one third. I said: Is the beggar the one who asks? He said: Yes, and the contented is the one who is satisfied with what you send to him of the piece of meat and more than that, and the beggar is the one who approaches you and does not ask you.

key_terms.الْقَانِعَ: the contented one (who accepts what is given)

ai.seo_question: How should an animal offering be distributed among family and different types of poor people according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates the tripartite distribution of the pilgrimage offering (hady) among the family, the contented poor, and the beggar, providing a nuanced jurisprudential distinction between the 'qani' who passively accepts charity and the 'miskeen' who actively solicits it. This classification reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on social stratification within the needy, ensuring that charity reaches both those who maintain dignity by not asking and those who require direct engagement to secure sustenance.

en.basel-kadem: 2.	With this chain of narrators, from Ali bin Mahziyar, from Hussain bin Sa’eed, from Safwan, from Saif, the Date Seller, that he said:

Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, said: Sa’eed bin Abdul-Malik came, as a pilgrim, and met my father, peace be upon him, and said: I dragged an (animal of) offering, so what do I do? He said: Feed your family a third, the needy a third, and the beggar a third. I said: Is the beggar the one who asks? He said: Yes, and the needy is the one who is content with what you send to him of the piece and what is above. The beggar is the one who approaches you (suddenly) and does not ask you.
